item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The current containment procedures confuse me. The Foundation knows it wants the Foundation. The Foundation knows it shouldn't feed it.

So why is the Foundation currently feeding it? They ought to take it someplace extremely isolated, like a remote controlled drone flying over Antarctica, and see how big that area of effect can get. If it's a biomass, it's expending energy to enlarge the area of effect. It can't keep it up forever. And it can't make the area of effect infinitely big, or else it would be doing that already.

So starve it. Stop feeding it. Even feeding it for five minutes is still feeding it.

Actually, the reason for the original phrasing is that people aren't supposed to know that Sigma-3 locates SCPs.

As the author, I'll go ahead and implement an alternate version of this crosslink. I'll copy the change in this post once I'm done so people can critique it separately if they wish.

EDIT: Added, before the addenda:

[SPECIAL ACCESS REQUIRED]
Access granted.

SCP-472 was located via reports from the so-called 'anomalous community', from interfacing with Mobile Task Force Sigma-3 ("Bibliographers"). Initial theories from anomalous community sources categorized SCP-472 as a 'seal' containing an entity responsible for SCP-472's anomalous effects. However, further analysis has not supported this, rather indicating that SCP-472's appearance as a red garnet may be due to an fundamental perception error of unknown nature. Sources have not able to confirm anything substantial about the origin or nature of SCP-472.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Crosslink implemented by author. See below for discussion.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So, this is a pretty self contained article as is, and I personally feel like trying to add a link to another article might mess with the flow (granted, maybe more skilled hands than mine could get it to work.) However, I noticed that in the very excellent Magic Orientation it is mentioned that Sigma-3 was the Foundation Investigation team that brought SCP-472 to the Foundation's attention. For this reason, a link between this article and that tale makes sense. As such, I am proposing the following edit:

Editing this:

SCP-472 was recovered from the mansion residence of [REDACTED], a wealthy man living in [REDACTED]. Foundation investigators were alerted by local reports of hauntings by domestic staff after [REDACTED] was hospitalized by a fall. Mobile Task Force Delta-5 ("Front Runners") was assigned to investigate due to possible connection to ongoing projects. Investigation narrowed down the origin of the anomalous effects to SCP-472, which had been prominently displayed in [REDACTED]'s jewel collection. Origin of SCP-472 is under investigation.

To this:

SCP-472 was recovered from the mansion residence of [REDACTED], a wealthy man living in [REDACTED]. Mobile Task Force Sigma-3 ("Bibliographers") were alerted by local reports of hauntings by domestic staff after [REDACTED] was hospitalized by a fall. Mobile Task Force Delta-5 ("Front Runners") was assigned to investigate due to possible connection to ongoing projects. Investigation narrowed down the origin of the anomalous effects to SCP-472, which had been prominently displayed in [REDACTED]'s jewel collection. Origin of SCP-472 is under investigation.

Its a simple inline edit, but it makes sense for the article, doesn't tinker with the narrative flow too much, and opens the reader to all the content for Sigma-3 produced during the MTF contest.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: Re: Uh.
item.content:encoded:
Well, see, it's sort of an error. Yes, 9.3 square meters is the same as 100 square feet. The thing is, it doesn't make sense for the containment procedures to specify the area of the room; in fact, they supposedly are determining the dimensions of the room. If it did so correctly, it would specify the length and width of the room, which it does not. It's an error I see a lot, and it bugs me quite a bit.

Seeing as how effects happen within 18 meters of 472, I say we scrap the whole square units thing and just have it in the center of a 37m x 37m room. Or, because that's rather excessive, it can be in a smaller room at the end of a long hallway or something. I'll leave it up to you, because it's less of a math thing and more of an author decision sort of thing.

Update: Made this no longer a sphere. Or a ruby. It's still a red rock, but I could change that too, frankly.

DrGuin: Unsure how to tweak the effect without getting rid of what people liked about the hallucinations. Probably because I'm still a little unclear on what they did like about the hallucinations. To me, the hallucinations themselves were incidental to the original piece, and it was mostly the idea of what effect it might have on someone that was interesting. But this is a rewrite, not an original work, and to me the point of a rewrite is to preserve what was liked about the article in the first place.

EDIT: If I was to tweak the effect further, I'd probably play up the 'heart' angle. Like, first you hear a heartbeat, then maybe by the end you're hallucinating a bunch of (ripped up?) blood vessels, arteries, veins, aortas, etc, all over the floor and walls. Oooor… twisted bloody apparitions based on your own Secret Desires. Or something else.

EDIT: OR OR it disappears people affected by it too long, and turns them into strange pulsing organs that make up some growing mass that is only visible when you start being affected by the early-stage hallucinations. But maybe that's getting to over the top. Hm.

item.content:encoded:
Further as to why I don't like the MC&D addition: It's not needed, and it doesn't seem logically congruent. As an item it doesn't seem like it would be very useful for MC&D or its clients, especially not so much that they would try to reclaim it. The guy who used it for interrogations and "sexual assaults" — eeesh.

This is really little more than a thing that makes you go crazy. Everyone else hates it for that reason, but I like it because to me it is a good example of the genre, so it doesn't need to do anything else but sit on its pedestal in containment and make the occasional D-class guinea pig see blood dripping from the walls.

The object itself hardly matters, but making it a blood red gemstone helps to tie it into that whole thumping heartbeat, melting reality thing. If I'd change anything it would just be to strip it down and get rid of the dialogue and leave the reader to imagine what it would be like to be stuck in a room with this thing in it.

I guess the scariest thought of this item would be if it was on display in a room somewhere and no one knew IT was the source of the problem. Slowly over a span of days anyone entering that room would hear the thumping, start seeing things… they'd flee, but sooner or later they'd have to go back. Maybe they were a maid who had to clean that damn room for some rich dude who never visited it.

Maybe if you can bring that kind of feeling to this other people would come around, like if you did a recovery log at the end that discussed the last victim's slow breakdown or reports of hauntings that they finally isolated to this one object.

I'd like for there to be more to the idea. May be just me, but even cliche points (provokes insanity, whatnot) can make a SCP completely awesome when there's more of a rhyme and reason to when they make people go insane. SCP-342 makes people act crazy because they see themselves on a train ride to hell. 882 makes people go insane in order to make itself larger, for whatever purpose it may have. 804's apparent mental compulsion stemmed from the fact that the people who made it actually wanted to put an end to the human race.

This is a rock that makes you see stuff.
